Independent complex-contour diagonalization tests the Bessis cubic spectrum.
The PT-symmetric and non-PT linear perturbations are solved independently and compared by reality and positivity.
The p^2+x^2+ix spectrum is derived by completing the square.
The p^2+x^2-x spectrum is derived by completing the square.
The p^2+x^2+ix-x complex spectrum is derived by a complex displacement.
Both wedge centers, opening and limiting angles are evaluated analytically.
Independent spectra on three admissible contour deformations are compared at N=3 and N=4.
Both printed turning points are substituted into E+(ix)^N=0 and their half-planes are checked.
The WKB segment's actual intersection with the imaginary axis determines whether it crosses the positive-imaginary branch cut above and below N=2.
The |x|^N WKB formula and square-well limit are checked with an independent Hermitian solver.
The Airy matching derivative is evaluated over several real energies.
A harmonic-basis two-level reduction verifies the negative non-Hermitian discriminant and high-level-first mergers.
The finite N>=2 period and N=2 harmonic anchor are evaluated analytically.

direct_gap_statements: The last three printed exact Table II values differ from both independent solvers by 0.000221, 0.003136 and 0.038445 while the first four rows agree at printed precision.

direct_cause.statement: The last three printed exact Table II values differ from both independent solvers by 0.000221, 0.003136 and 0.038445 while the first four rows agree at printed precision.

root_cause.statement: Protocol-v2 fresh-context review independently confirmed that the stable mismatch is a paper-error candidate after parameter, convergence, implementation and analytic checks. The final publication-side cause remains unresolved without the authors' numerical record or another independent high-precision source, so this is not promoted to a confirmed paper error.

code_fault_assessment.statement: No reproduction-code defect was found: Riccati shooting and a distinct finite-difference eigenproblem agree, both converge with domain/resolution, and analytic/table anchors pass.

checks.statement: All seven epsilon values, the Hamiltonian and Table II comparator are bound to the printed paper parameters.
Changing the shooting boundary from 40 to 30 changes the energies by at most 1.59e-8.
Riccati shooting and sparse finite differences agree within 1.83e-5 over the complete epsilon grid.
The independently evaluated Eq. (11) roots match the printed asymptotic column and the exact first four rows match the paper at its declared precision.
